QUEUE_SIZE.description: The maximum log size sent to client, <=0 means no limit

USE_YOUTUBE_DL.description: Use yt-dlp instead of the Node.js audio stream

USE_NATIVE_FETCH.description: Download through the Rust fetcher (amhra-fetch) instead of yt-dlp

NATIVE_FETCH_BIN.description: Path to the amhra-fetch binary; defaults to rust/target/release/amhra-fetch

USE_RUST_VOICE.description: Play through the Rust voice sidecar instead of @discordjs/voice

NATIVE_NO_CACHE.description: With USE_RUST_VOICE, stream tracks straight into voice without writing them to the cache; each track is held in memory only while it plays

NATIVE_VOICE_BIN.description: Path to the amhra-sidecar binary; defaults to rust/target/release/amhra-sidecar

CROSSFADE_IN_MS.description: Overlap between one track and the next in milliseconds; 0 is a hard cut (Rust voice path only)

SKIP_FADE_IN_MS.description: Overlap when a listener skips, in milliseconds; kept short so a skip feels immediate

SEEK.description: Enable time seeking function, should be closed when using youtube-dl

AUTO_LEAVE.description: Time in ms before auto leave

AUTO_LEAVE_ALONE.description: Time in ms before leaving a voice channel nobody else is in (negative disables)

MAX_CACHE_IN_GB.description: Maximum video cache in GB, only be used when USE_YOUTUBE_DL is set to TRUE

MAX_REPLAY_BUFFER_IN_SEC.description: Seconds of already-played audio kept in memory for instant backward seek; beyond this the cache file is re-read. Default 30

MAX_STREAM_BUFFER_IN_MB.description: Memory budget per stream for not-yet-played audio; past it packets are dropped and re-read from the cache file. Bounds livestreams. Default 34 (~30min of audio)

AUTO_SCHEDULE_PREMIERES.description: Schedule an upcoming premiere to cut in when it starts instead of refusing it when played (default true)

LYRICS_DELAY_MS.description: Shift synced lyrics by this many milliseconds; positive shows each line later, negative sooner. The default for songs without their own delay, which is set per song from /lyrics or the dashboard (default 0)

VOICE_COMMANDS.description: Let servers turn on voice commands ("Amhra, skip"). Needs USE_RUST_VOICE, a sidecar built with --features voice-commands and the models from scripts/download-voice-models.sh; loads about 570MB of models. Restart to apply

VOICE_WAKE_MODEL.description: Directory of the fine-tuned wake model; defaults to models/voice/kws-emhara. Restart to apply

VOICE_WAKE_KEYWORDS.description: Wake phrases for that model; defaults to training/wake/keywords.txt. Restart to apply

VOICE_WAKE_CLASSIFIER.description: Directory of the wake word classifier from training/wake/classifier/export.py (e.g. models/voice/wake-classifier), to hear the bot's name with instead of the wake model; VOICE_WAKE_MODEL and VOICE_WAKE_KEYWORDS are then unused. Unset by default (experimental). Restart to apply

VOICE_COLLECT_WAKE_CLIPS.description: Save the second or so of audio each time the bot hears its name, in servers with voice commands on, to data/recordings/wake-clips for retraining the wake model. Members are told when it is on. Default on. Restart to apply

VOICE_LOG_TRANSCRIPTS.description: Log what was heard after the bot's name, for tuning the command matching. Off by default: it writes what people said into the log

VOICE_SPEECH.description: Say aloud what a voice command does ("Skipping.", "Playing bad guy.") in the command's language, over the lowered music: English, Japanese and Korean with Supertonic 3, Mandarin with Kokoro, Cantonese with a VITS voice, whichever scripts/download-voice-models.sh --speech fetched. Fixed phrases are made once and saved under the cache; a song name takes about half a second of CPU on a fast machine and a few on a Raspberry Pi. Default off. Restart to apply

VOICE_SPEECH_THREADS.description: CPU threads for making speech. More makes a new phrase sooner but takes cores from playback and recognition. Restart to apply

VOICE_SPEECH_PROVIDER.description: Where speech is made, with the same needs as VOICE_RECOGNISER_PROVIDER. On an M5 Pro, coreml made Supertonic 15 to 20% slower and the Cantonese voice no faster, and gains Kokoro nothing. Restart to apply

VOICE_WAKE_CHIME.description: Chime in the call when the bot hears its name. Default on. Restart to apply

VOICE_DUCK_VOLUME.description: Music volume, as a fraction, from when the bot hears its name until the command has been heard. Default 0.3; 1 leaves the music alone. Restart to apply

VOICE_RECOGNISER_PROVIDER.description: Where speech recognition runs. coreml needs a sidecar built with --features shared-onnxruntime on macOS, gpu (CUDA) one built with --features cuda-onnxruntime against a sherpa-onnx GPU release; otherwise it says so and stays on cpu. coreml measured slower than cpu on this model. Restart to apply

VOICE_WAKE_PROVIDER.description: Where the keyword spotter that hears the name runs, with the same needs as VOICE_RECOGNISER_PROVIDER. It runs every 20ms for everyone speaking, so cpu is usually fastest. The wake classifier only runs on cpu. Restart to apply

VOICE_RECOGNISER_THREADS.description: Threads for speech recognition; more makes each command faster (4 roughly halves it). Restart to apply

VOICE_LANGUAGE.description: The language voice commands are heard in, in every server. auto guesses per command and sometimes takes a short one for another language; pinned, commands in other languages are not understood. Restart to apply

VOICE_WAIT_FOR_COMMAND_MS.description: How long after the name to wait for a command to start, in milliseconds. A pause before the command, waiting for the chime, does not end it within this time. Applies at once, from the next time the name is heard

VOICE_END_SILENCE_MS.description: Silence that ends a command, in milliseconds. Longer forgives pauses mid-command; every millisecond is added to the wait for an answer. Applies at once, to commands already being heard too

VOICE_MAX_COMMAND_MS.description: The longest command, in milliseconds, from just before the name ended. Applies at once, to commands already being heard too

VOICE_INTENT_MODEL_URL.description: An OpenAI-compatible server on this machine (mlx_lm.server, LM Studio, Ollama), as http://host:port/v1, whose language model decides what each voice command asks for. Empty, or when the server does not answer within 3 seconds: only a command's own name said first ("skip", "play <song>") is understood

VOICE_INTENT_MODEL.description: The model that server should use for voice commands

VOICE_INTENT_PROVIDER.description: Where the server the bot starts runs the voice command model. cpu: llama.cpp's llama-server with nothing on the GPU, on Apple silicon too instead of MLX, so a VOICE_INTENT_MODEL naming an MLX model will not load. gpu: everything on the GPU. coreml: neither runtime has it, so cpu. Unset: MLX on Apple silicon, llama.cpp's own choice elsewhere. A server the bot did not start is left as it is. Restart to apply
